Approach: Try olmoearth_scores_from_file with run_dir "F4/emsr279-11"? That would guess the directory name — risky. The answer to "which is correct": without labels, not resolvable — the tool explicitly states it cannot say which side is correct; if there's no label, decline and explain why. result.class_pairs_reading: class_pairs counts, for each unordered pair of classes, the windows where one map has one class and the other map the other, both directions together; 'directions' splits that count by which map has which class, as class_changes does.
result.listing_order: the 10 listed windows are the first differing windows in window order (from row 0), not a sample of them; all 1,570 are in the file compare_differing_eec2555155.json, in the same order. Read which classes change, in which direction and where from class_changes, class_pairs, spatial and facts, not from the list. review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows

spatial.reading: Each band is a strip of whole rows (row_bands) or whole columns (col_bands) of the window grid, numbered from 0: row band 0 holds row 0, the grid's first rows, and column band 0 holds column 0; the scores carry no georeference (no window locations or transform), so the rows need not run north to south and no band is a compass direction. share_of_differing is the band's share of ALL differing windows; share_of_windows is its share of all compared windows, the share an even spread would give it; share_of_band_differing is the share of the band's own windows that differ. top_band_share is row band 0's share_of_differing; max_band is the band, of either axis, holding the most differing windows.

facts.sentence: The most common change is class 0 (not water) in map A to class 1 (water) in map B: 1,247 of the 1,570 differing windows (79.4%); the reverse, class 1 (water) in map A to class 0 (not water) in map B, is 323 (20.6%).

no labels were given to this comparison, which takes none: nothing here says which map is right, more accurate or better, and nothing here says whether labels for these maps exist (none was looked up); neither map is shown right where they differ, and the more confident side is not thereby the right one

labels drawn only from the low-confidence, least certain or most ambiguous windows (or from a review set) are not a sample of the map: an error rate over them describes those windows and overstates the map's, so it is no defensible error rate for either map; each of olmoearth_plan_label_sample's designs ('confidence', 'proportional', 'random') draws from every window of the map, and its estimate needs every drawn window labelled

content:
## Comparison of maps A vs B

Compared all 78,028 shared windows; **1,570 differ (2.0%)**. The maps describe dates 216 days apart, so any difference could be real ground change or an error in one map.

**Direction of change:**

| Direction | Windows | Share of differing |
|---|---|---|
| A not water -> B water | 1,247 | 79.4% |
| A water -> B not water | 323 | 20.6% |

- **Confidence:** Map A has the larger margin on 77.6% of the differing windows (B on 22.4%) — but a larger margin does not make A right.
- **Where:** differences concentrate in rows 2800-4199 (the grid's 50-75% band), which holds 46.8% of all differing windows; scores carry no georeference, so rows need not run north-south. All 1,570 differing windows are listed in `compare_differing_eec2555155.json` (path above).

**Which side is right?** Neither can be graded from this comparison. A difference across these two dates either reflects change on the ground (seasonal cycles included) or an error in one map, and the decisions alone cannot separate the two. Each map needs a reference dated to its own date: labels for 2017 grade only map A, labels for 2018 only map B. If you have reference data for either (or both) dates, I can plan a label sample per map with `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` and then estimate each map's error rate.
